frozen_by: not frozen; the freeze follows the external read-only review (M3-PLAN.md §2 N1)
description: Expected outcomes for gatebraid/evidence-capture@1, the third frozen interface — which shipped at N1 with no fixtures at all, the same gap the N1 internal review found in metrics@1. Every invalid case is a SINGLE mutation of its NEAREST VALID SIBLING, named per case: valid-argv-capture.json for most, valid-shell-capture-declared.json for EC1-07/25, valid-cp936-lossy-decode.json for EC1-08/09/12, valid-with-outputs.json for EC1-18. Every expectation was MEASURED with CPython 3.12.2 / jsonschema 4.23.0; `required` expectations additionally record WHICH property is missing, derived from the validator's own per-property error rather than written by hand (M3 batch N1C, A3). Byte streams carry REAL bytes: base64, byte_length and sha256 are computed from the content, and the cp936 rendering in EC1-03 was produced by letting the decode raise and recording CPython's own exception text and offset. The schema cannot check those relations and says so; N3 will. An internally incoherent fixture would be a bad fixture regardless of what the schema can see.
known_limitation: THREE limitations, all MEASURED at M3 batch N1C by sweeping every corpus for identical expected-locus sets. (1) COLLIDING LOCUS SETS REMAIN, and an earlier draft of this note both understated their number and mis-called the one it did name irreducible. Measured, across all three corpora: EC1-09/EC1-10 share required@streams/stdout/rendered:text — separable by schema path (EC1-09 -> properties/streams/properties/stdout/properties/rendered/allOf/2/then/required; EC1-10 -> properties/streams/properties/stdout/properties/rendered/allOf/3/then/required); EC1-11/EC1-12 share not@streams/stdout/rendered — separable by schema path (EC1-11 -> properties/streams/properties/stdout/properties/rendered/allOf/3/then/not; EC1-12 -> properties/streams/properties/stdout/properties/rendered/allOf/1/then/not); EC1-28/EC1-29 share pattern@streams/stdout/data — NOT separable by schema path (EC1-28 -> properties/streams/properties/stdout/properties/data/pattern; EC1-29 -> properties/streams/properties/stdout/properties/data/pattern); MT1-05/MT1-08 share not@metrics/0 — separable by schema path (MT1-05 -> properties/metrics/items/allOf/0/else/not; MT1-08 -> properties/metrics/items/allOf/2/then/not). Three of these are separable by the error's `absolute_schema_path`, which the runner already holds on every error object; only the pair failing the SAME constraint on two different values is irreducible by any locus refinement. Extending the locus tuple to carry the schema path is a change to a committed runner beyond this batch's A3 scope and is escalated, not taken. (2) `ended_at >= started_at` REMAINS unenforceable: it compares two sibling properties and no JSON Schema keyword relates one instance value to another, so a capture whose end precedes its start validates here and must be rejected by N3's re-derivation — recorded in the schema's own `ended_at` description as that duty. (3) The timestamp patterns enforce RFC3339 LEXICAL FORM only: field ranges are unchecked, so a month of 13, an hour of 99 or an offset of +99:99 matches, as does a calendar-invalid date. Measured, not assumed. SCOPE NOTE ON THE RULING: the approval names 'the four timestamp fields'; `gatebraid/evidence-capture@1` carries TWO date-time fields. Read as the four CONSTRAINTS the correct-course names — both timestamps plus binary_mode_write and zero_lone_cr.asserted — which is the only reading under which the count is four, and which produces EC1-34 through EC1-37. Recorded rather than applied silently. Those four are now falsified; `format: date-time` was removed from both timestamp fields rather than retained as an annotation, because a validator built with a FormatChecker on a host carrying rfc3339_validator emits an additional `format` locus and the corpus's own equality check would then fail.
